name: BAP1
summary: BAP1 is a tumour suppressor frequently inactivated in pleural mesothelioma; loss of nuclear BAP1 immunostaining supports a diagnosis of mesothelioma over reactive mesothelial proliferation, and germline variants define the BAP1 tumour predisposition syndrome.
biology: BAP1 is a nuclear deubiquitinase (removing monoubiquitin from histone H2A as part of the polycomb repressive deubiquitinase complex) involved in chromatin regulation, DNA repair and cell death pathways. Biallelic inactivation by deletion, mutation or splice alteration is a common event in mesothelioma, particularly the epithelioid subtype.
alterations: Somatic biallelic inactivation (deletions, truncating mutations, splice variants)
Germline pathogenic variants (BAP1 tumour predisposition syndrome)

methods: Immunohistochemistry for loss of nuclear BAP1 expression
Germline testing on blood for suspected predisposition
testing.specimen: Formalin-fixed paraffin-embedded tissue or cytology cell block; peripheral blood for germline testing
testing.notes: Retained nuclear BAP1 does not exclude mesothelioma. Loss of BAP1 with or without MTAP loss/CDKN2A deletion supports malignancy in an atypical mesothelial proliferation, including in situ mesothelioma.

predictiveRelevance: BAP1 is principally a diagnostic biomarker; no BAP1-directed therapy is established. Associations with response to platinum, EZH2 inhibition, PARP inhibition and immunotherapy have been explored without definitive predictive evidence. Germline carriers warrant genetic counselling and surveillance for associated cancers (uveal and cutaneous melanoma, renal cell carcinoma, mesothelioma).
